Samira — great to hear the demo landed well. High-level answers below and I attached a short pricing matrix for the tiers (redwood_pricing_matrix_Q2_2027.csv).

1) Credits vs on-demand: for workloads ~1B+ tokens/month we generally recommend committing to a monthly credits bundle (examples in the CSV). Committed bundles unlock two levers: a per-token discount and access to a discounted quantized model variant (q4_8 or q5_sm) that gets you 15–25% unit cost reduction while preserving quality in our benchmarks. The biggest incremental savings come from pairing a commit with "dynamic batching" enabled in the route — that reduces tail cost for bursty traffic.

2) Quantization recommendations: we include a recommended quantization profile and validation checklist as part of the Optimize toolkit subscription (no extra charge for recommendations). If you want Redwood to run the in-production quantization pilot and guardrails (side-by-side evals, regen tests, histogram of token deltas), that is a short professional-services engagement (1–2 weeks) — typical SKU: "Quant Pilot" — ballpark $12k–18k depending on model size and runtime. I summarized this in the attached memo (quant_recommendation_memo.pdf).

Procurement target: we can structure a 12-month commit with a 20% off baseline if you commit to >= 12M tokens/month equivalent and sign by EOM April — otherwise our standard committed discount is 12–15% for the mid-tier. Doing a credits + pilot bundle makes it easier to justify the higher discount.

If useful I can put together a mutual action plan and SOW draft (EdgeFin_SOW_v1.pdf) for review.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachment: quant_recommendation_memo.pdf (summary of profiles and pilot scope)

Karthik — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. A few clarifying points from our side:  

- We can likely scale to the 12M tokens/month equivalent in a 12-month commit if the unit economics hold, but procurement needs a clear SOW that separates the platform commit from the quant pilot fees so CFO can model cashflow.
- We need explicit language around fallback policies: if the quantized variant causes a measurable regression on our primary customer prompt set, what's the rollback and support SLA?
- Can you confirm whether the discounted quantized variant is supported on Dedicated and Private deployments or only on Hosted? Our security team is leaning Private.

If you can send a short mutual action plan with a line-itemized quote and a DocuSign-ready SOW, procurement will prioritize.

Samira

Subject: Fwd: Optimize toolkit — packaging & quantization questions

Laura/Monica — looping you both in to propose the specific commercial structure. Quick suggested approach below (I also plan to push a draft SOW to Samira after we agree):

Proposal (short):
- 12-month credits commitment at 12M tokens/month equivalent (pre-paid monthly billing option).
- Baseline 18% committed discount on token price + additional 4% if we include the Quant Pilot within 30 days (conditional credit). Total 22% off list on tokens if pilot accepted.
- Quant Pilot: $14k fixed fee (1–2 week engagement) — separate line item in SOW for CFO clarity. Pilot includes regression suite (customer prompt set), rollback plan, and one production rollback window included.
- SLA/rollback: If regression delta > 2.5% on agreed eval metric, Redwood will (a) pause quantized route, (b) revert clients to float variant within target rollback SLA = 2 business hours, (c) include 1 week of priority tuning sessions. Add this as an appendix.
- Deployment support: discounted quantized variants supported on Hosted and Dedicated today; Private requires a short validation step and a compatibility check (low friction but note in SOW). Recommend adding a 30-day Private compatibility clause with a one-time acceptance test (no extra software fee).

Questions for you both:  
- Are these discounts within the channel playbook? Is the combined 22% (18% baseline + 4% pilot) acceptable?
- Do we want to include a 3% early-signing credit for signing within 10 business days to hit procurement's EOM ask?

I propose we send Samira a one-page mutual action plan and attach EdgeFin_SOW_v1.pdf with the line items separated.

—K
